transcript.text: Thanks, Maya. Since it seems like others may not have specific concerns to add right now, I'll go ahead and share what I've been holding. I've seen some of the same patterns people are describing — interruptions during discussion, and exercises that felt improvised rather than planned. I think there are a couple of concrete things I can contribute to the facilitation question. I'd be willing to step in as a neutral timekeeper for the first several sessions after the current facilitator leaves — say the first six — to help us establish a more structured rhythm while we figure out a longer-term solution. That would pair well with Renee's point about having written prompts in advance: if we build in a timekeeper role and a commitment to circulating materials 48 hours ahead, we'd be addressing the structure and predictability concerns directly. I also think it's worth noting that the interruption pattern isn't just a feeling — I've observed it happening on multiple occasions this quarter. So building in some norms around how we handle speaking turns might be worth considering too. But I don't want to get ahead of the group — these are suggestions, and I'm open to other approaches.
